title: Letter 7 — On the Soul's Bitter Medicine
attribution_note: Letter 7 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: A bitter medicine for the soul

pairs.en: *“My friend and companion!”*

You asked me to write you something touching the profit of the soul. I commend your desire, and wish that such a desire may dwell always in your heart. But since I myself am poor and needy, I take from the Psalms of David, as from a saving spiritual pharmacy, medicine that is useful to our souls, and this I send to you. It is bitter, but profitable to the soul. Salt is bitter, but it drives out worms and keeps matter from corruption; and medicine, bitter though it be, we take nonetheless, that the body may be healed. Such as bitter salt and bitter medicine are, such is the word of rebuke to a sinful soul, which is directed against the sins, and not against the soul itself — just as every medicine attacks the sickness, and not the man, and salt destroys the corruption and the worms, but not the matter itself that the salt has been applied to.

Receive, then, beloved, this medicine, and apply it to your soul. And according to what she is sick with, apply the medicine fitted to that sickness, and apply it until the sickness has gone out. Understand what I write, and may the Lord give you understanding.

sections.heading: What God says to the sinner

pairs.en: There, that is, in the Psalms, it is sung: *“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence”* [Psalm 49:21]. Who says this? God. To whom? To the sinner, as was said above in the same psalm [Psalm 49:16]. What does it mean, “These things hast thou done”? It refers to what was said just before, namely: “But thou,” O sinner, *“hatest instruction, and castest My words behind thee.* *When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers.* *Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.* *Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son”* [Psalm 49:17–20]. This, then, is what this word of God to the sinner means: “These things hast thou done.” That is: thou, O sinner, hast despised My words, given thee for thy correction — the very words thou oughtest always to hold before thee, to honour and love as the words of My own mouth, and by whose rule to correct thy life — thou hast utterly cast them away, and so hast lived lawlessly: stolen, committed adultery, belched out malice, flattered with thy mouth and thy tongue, slandered thy brother, and given occasion of offence, and the rest. “These things hast thou done.”

What further does God say to the sinner? “— And I kept silence. —” What does this mean, “and I kept silence”? That is: thou, O sinner, didst these deeds and these iniquities, and I saw them; I saw, but held My peace, waiting for thy conversion, thy repentance and thy correction — but thou remainest uncorrected, as thou wast before; thou doest evil, as thou didst before; thou sinnest, as thou didst before; thou livest lawlessly, as thou didst before; thou rejectest My words, as thou didst reject them before, and despisest them, as thou didst despise them before; thou stealest, committest adultery, art malicious, flatterest, slanderest and givest offence, as thou didst before; and thou dost not cease to do evil.

What further, then, does God say to the sinner? Listen: *“Thou thoughtest that I was altogether such a one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”* [Psalm 49:21]. Thinkest thou that the transgression of My law shall pass thee by unpunished? No, thou art deceived, and thou dost delude thyself! It shall not be as thou blindly dreamest.

Sayest thou in thy heart that this shall not be required of thee [Psalm 9:34]? No! All thy sins and thy iniquities are numbered and written down before Me, and all that thou didst secretly shall be uncovered, and all that thou hast done in word, deed and thought shall be set before thee. “I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” And the holy apostle likewise says: *“the Lord... will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts”* [1 Corinthians 4:5].

What follows upon that dreadful rebuke? The apostle answers, and says to the lawless: *“Be not deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God”* [1 Corinthians 6:9–10]. And again: *“the works of the flesh are manifest, which are these: Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lasciviousness, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, variance, emulations, wrath, strife, seditions, heresies, envyings, murders, drunkenness, revellings, and such like: of the which I tell you before, as I have also told you in time past, that they which do such things shall not inherit the kingdom of God”* [Galatians 5:19–21]. What place, then, shall be theirs, if they shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Christ the Lord determines it for them: *“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death”* [Revelation 21:8]. And the holy Forerunner likewise said: *“And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire”* [Matthew 3:10; Luke 3:9]. This, then, is what awaits those who despise the Word of God and His holy law: judgment, and condemnation to everlasting fire [Matthew 25:41].

But let us hear further what David sings on in his psalm: *“Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver”* [Psalm 49:22]. Who must consider this? Those who forget God, transgressing His holy law without fear. What must they consider? This: that He will reprove the transgressors of His law in all their sins, and will render to every one of them according to his deeds. Therefore, “consider this,” and come to your senses, repent, and amend yourselves, lest, remaining uncorrected, His righteous judgment “tear you in pieces,” and then “there be none to deliver” you. Neither the rich man's riches, nor the glorious man's glory and honour, nor the strong man's strength, nor the noble man's nobility, nor the wise man's wisdom, nor the cunning man's cunning, nor friend for friend, nor brother for brother, nor father for son, nor son for father, shall deliver — man shall not deliver man. *“A brother doth not redeem: shall a man at all redeem? he shall not give to God a ransom for himself”* [Psalm 48:8]. Here, then, brother, is a bitter medicine for you, but such a one as drives the rotten, long-standing humours out of the soul.

What, then, will deliver the sinner from the judgment of God? David shows it by his own example in the very next psalm, the fiftieth, crying to God from the depths of his heart: *“Have mercy upon me, O God, according to Thy great mercy,”* and the rest. That is: true repentance, joined to faith in Christ the Son of God, the Redeemer, delivers the sinner from judgment. Such a one *“shall not come into judgment, but shall pass from death unto life,”* says Christ [John 5:24].

But whoever would appease God by repentance and be delivered from judgment must no longer provoke Him — that is, he must leave off his sins, since it is by these that God is provoked; otherwise, if the sins are not left off, the repentance will be false, and not true. There are no sins, and no number of sins, that would not be forgiven by God to a sinner who truly repents. The divine Blood of Christ cleanses every sin, and makes clean the one who truly repents, and gratefully receives Him in faith as his Redeemer, his Deliverer and his Saviour [Ezekiel 33:11–12, 15–16; Isaiah 43:25; Micah 7:19; Acts 10:43; 1 John 1:7; 2:2; Luke 24:47; Romans 5:20].

Be comforted by this, O repenting soul, and apply it, as a healing plaster, to your bruised and wounded heart. One thing alone remains to the sinner: to turn from his sins to God, and to bring Him true repentance and sorrow, that by them he has so foolishly provoked his Creator and Benefactor; and so henceforth to stand firm, and to strive against every sin, and to take heed lest, in word, deed or evil thought, he provoke his Lord. *“But with the Lord there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption”* [Psalm 129:6].

Here, then, I send you, brother, what is profitable to my soul, as also to yours, and which “is the one thing needful,” in the word of our Saviour [Luke 10:42]. For only eternal salvation is needful to us, so that without it there is no profit, though we should gain the whole world. *“For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”* says the Lord [Matthew 16:26; Mark 8:36].

Let us admit, then, beloved, this rebuking Word of God into our hearts, and let us root it deep within them, that we may drive out from there all uncleanness and corruption, and prepare the heart to receive the living comfort of the Gospel. For whoever would be found worthy of God's mercy must without fail turn away from sin, and crush his heart with sorrow for his sins. Let us repent, then, and appease our God, that our sins may be blotted out, that they may not appear with us at the dread Judgment of Christ, that the Judge may not say of any one of us then: “Behold the man, and his deeds!” Let us write this word of God — “I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes” — let us write it upon our memory, that it may always sound within us, whenever our enemy would incite us to any sin.

Now God says to the sinner: “I will reprove thee” — that he may repent, and that then He may not have to reprove him. But if he does not repent, He will most certainly reprove him then, and will say: “Behold the man, and his deeds!” Now He threatens sinners, that they may repent and be saved, for He is good and loves mankind; but then He will fulfil the threat in the very deed against those who have not repented. Now He says to sinners, “Repent”; but then He will say, “Answer Me!” Now He calls sinners to Himself: “Come unto Me” — but then He will answer sinners: “Depart from Me! Ye knew Me not while ye were in the world, and I know you not now. Ye did not listen to Me then, when I exhorted you and desired to save you, and I do not listen to you now, when ye pray. Depart from Me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels” [Matthew 25:41].

Oh, how dreadful will this voice be to sinners! So that they will then cry out to the mountains and the rocks: *“Fall on us, and hide us from the face of Him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: for the great day of His wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand”* [Revelation 6:16; Luke 23:29–30]? Let us fear now this dreadful voice, that we may not hear it then. *“Turn us again, O God, and cause Thy face to shine, and we shall be saved”* [Psalm 79:20].

sections.heading: Four things for the repenting sinner

pairs.en: If the sinner begins to repent, and to abstain from sin, he must do the following:
1) Comfort himself with the mercy of God, that God will have mercy on him, even as He has had mercy on other repenting sinners, and has mercy still.
2) Read Christian books, and learn wherein sin consists and wherein virtue, that he may be able to guard against sin and be taught virtue.
3) Pray often, that God Himself would give him understanding and enlighten him, and teach him to do what is pleasing to Him, and keep him from every sin.
4) And conduct himself carefully, that he not be caught by Satan; and so forth.
Read this, and share it with your brethren.
Be saved in Christ!
